outputs.explanation: This is a scatter plot in which each of the 141 points represents a single sample/measurement (rhythmicity index vs. period), so individual data points are inherently displayed. The accompanying marginal histograms show distributions of these raw values, not group averages. Scatter plots are exempt from requiring additional overlay of individual points.

Each plotted point represents an average (mean ± s.d. across 6 replicates per reporter, or fewer as noted) of circadian/noise components for a given cell line, shown with error bars. This is a summary-statistic plot (akin to a mean±SD plot) rather than a raw-data scatter, and the underlying individual replicate values are not overlaid, so readers cannot assess the spread of the raw measurements behind each average.

These are density/distribution curves (line plots) of subtype-averaged periods and amplitudes. Line/density plots are exempt from requiring individual point overlays, as adding raw points would make the smoothed distributions unreadable.

This is a box plot of CWT ridge lengths, which already conveys the data distribution via quartiles, whiskers, median, and outliers. Box plots are exempt from the individual-data-point requirement; the panel additionally shows individual sample dots overlaid on the boxes, further supporting adequate representation of underlying data.

Polar histograms depicting the distribution of Bmal1-Per2 phase differences per cell line. Like other histogram/distribution plots, they inherently represent the spread of the underlying data and are exempt from requiring additional individual point overlays.

Polar histogram summarizing phase-difference distributions across subtypes (averaged from the cell-line-level histograms in panel E, whose individual n values are reported there). As a histogram-type distribution plot, it is exempt from needing individual point overlays.

This panel shows a single example signal (original trace, fitted sinusoidal model, and decay envelope) to illustrate the fitting procedure. It is an illustrative single-sample example rather than an averaged/aggregated summary of multiple samples, so the individual-data-point requirement does not apply.

Scatter plot in which each of the 117 points is an individual sample's fitted amplitude and decay rate; the error bars reflect the statistical uncertainty of each individual fit (not variability across averaged replicates). Since each point already is an individual measurement, this scatter plot is exempt from requiring further point overlays.
